tasks.title: Rivals who cooperate
tasks.html:
📖 Rivals who cooperate

We tend to assume competition and cooperation are opposites. In business, however, the most successful companies often do both at once. Working together — even with a rival — can save costs, share skills and knowledge, open new markets and help firms grow.
So why don’t rivals cooperate more? Many fear sharing will hand a competitor a competitive edge. The solution: set clear goals and agree exactly what can and cannot be shared. Examples include Ericsson, Uber, Toyota, Hulu, the Human Genome Project and Timberland. For many firms, cooperating with a rival is a no-brainer — provided everyone is on the same page about the limits.
